title: NetBench: domain adaptation for networking LLMs
tagline: What does domain adaptation teach a language model about high-performance networking?
summary: A 242-question benchmark built from 175 open-access papers, and a controlled study of 8 open-weight models (1B–27B) under fine-tuning, continued pre-training, and retrieval. Two LLM judges score every answer, a two-expert human study validates the primary judge, and one command regenerates every reported number.
short: Benchmark and controlled study of LLM domain adaptation for high-performance networking: 242 questions from 175 papers, 8 open-weight models (1B–27B) under fine-tuning, continued pre-training, and retrieval, two LLM judges validated by a human study, and one-command reproduction of every number.

title: Guarded orchestration for scientific models
tagline: Letting scientists run trained prediction models through natural language without the model guessing missing inputs.
summary: Extends LLM function calling with explicit workflow state. Inputs accumulate across turns, arguments are checked against typed schemas, and nothing runs until the required state is complete. Corrections, what-if questions, and resets are explicit state transitions.
short: State-aware layer over LLM function calling that accumulates inputs across turns, checks arguments against typed schemas, and blocks execution until the required state is complete; instantiated for protein-corona prediction.

title: Agentic Data Transfer Optimizer
tagline: Tuning bulk data transfers from live TCP telemetry, with the agent's actions kept inside hard limits.
status: In progress · prototype built, evaluation under way
summary: A Diagnostic agent and a Decision agent read live TCP telemetry, including congestion window, retransmissions, and RTT variance, and adjust transfer concurrency each interval. The system enforces hard limits, bounded changes, and oscillation damping around every recommendation.
short: Diagnostic and Decision agents tune transfer concurrency from live TCP telemetry over zero-copy sendfile() workers, inside hard limits with bounded changes and oscillation damping.
